narr: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms the 2nd through the 4th brought high winds, flooding, and some landspout tornadoes to the combined Panhandles. June 2nd brought high winds and flooding to both the Oklahoma and Texas Panhandle. The moisture continued into the 3rd and 4th but with slower moving storms and residual outflow boundaries from the 2nd storms produced heavy long lasting rainfall, as well as landspout tornadoes to the TX Panhandle. One landspout did touch down in Amarillo causing some damage. One of the boundaries that helped produce that landspout also caused storms to linger around Amarillo causing some historic flooding with the city having to pump water out of local playa and storm collection lakes well into July.
ev: Numerous road closures occurred across the city due to flash flooding. Playa lakes were overflowing onto roads and water rescues occurred with dive teams deployed. Several reports were relayed from Amarillo police department and Amarillo fire department.
Multiple road closures occurred in Canyon due to fast flowing water over roads. Reports were relayed from emergency management and canyon police department.
Multiple reports of several roads came in for having water over the road.
Three high water rescues occurred at the US Highways 87 and 60 interchange in Canyon. Hospital Drive, Hunsley Hills Boulevard, and Country Club Drive were all closed as well.
Social media pictures and video indicated fast moving water flowing down a residential street. Emergency management reported an estimated three feet of water in some spots on the southside of Pampa.
